claims.statement: Accepted bridge documents decode to the expected DTR model and rejected documents preserve the expected frontend diagnostic.
Supported DTR expressions, statements, bodies, reactions, instances, and complete core models translate to the expected LF structures.
The declared Lean modules establish the mapped translation and semantic correspondence obligations inside the verified boundary.
Registered translator fixtures traverse their declared source-to-target stages and reproduce committed artifacts.
Generated LF accepted by the pinned LF compiler provides target-compilation evidence; successful execution provides only the declared runtime observation.
Negative cases identify the component that rejects the input, preserve its diagnostic, and prohibit downstream artifacts.
RMC results are independent source-model evidence and are not evidence that the ReLico translation is correct.
Application benchmarks demonstrate corpus applicability and remain separate from translator conformance cases and formal obligations.

reporting_rules: A passing stage supports only the observation stated for that stage and claim.
Target compilation and process exit do not by themselves establish source-target behavioral equivalence.
Trusted-component integration evidence does not extend the verified Lean boundary.
Claims, logical cases, formal obligations, and application benchmarks are non-additive populations.
